paper: Scorecard of AI Evaluation Quality (San Joaquin, Gipiskis, Chin — Feb 2026)
scoring_note: Each dimension scored 1 (best) to 4 (worst), following the paper. Classification = the category implied by the weakest dimension (the paper caps a benchmark at its lowest-scoring dimension). Working draft — self-assessment, not an independent third-party grade.

satisfied: Hypothesis + operational failure definition pre-specified before running
Canonical 22-task dataset with T-CTRL-01/02 single-agent controls
Error analysis on the gpt-oss parsing bug (28%->0%)
gaps: block/clarify/proceed rubric conflates 'avoided unsafe action' with 'added friction' — no sub-component split
construct_validity.justification: Strong on pre-specification and controls; weakened by an action rubric that does not separate 'did the safe thing' from 'added friction', the same ambiguity flagged in the first Make-Me-Pay eval.

satisfied: Live Together AI inference (real model, not mocked)
temperature=0; state cleared between task runs
gaps: Pilot N=1 per (model, task, phase); no power calculation or SE estimates — a floor item per the paper
internal_validity.justification: Real inference helps, but N=1 per cell with no uncertainty estimate is the paper's internal-validity floor failure. N>=3 per cell is the single biggest lever.

satisfied: Real Malaysian banking domain grounded in BNM RMiT / PDPA
Live inference is one genuine deployment condition
gaps: Only 2 of 4 pre-registered deployment conditions implemented (clean baseline + compliance-forcing; protective Bedrock-XML overlay and neutral-persona condition open)
external_validity.justification: Domain grounding is good; coverage of deployment conditions is partial, so external validity is capped below the published-benchmark level.

satisfied: Fixed the gpt-oss reasoning-token truncation bug
Fisher's exact, Cohen's h, Bonferroni correction reported
gaps: No replication_config.json (pinned API versions, seed, judge prompt) committed
reliability.justification: Statistical hygiene present, but the paper treats missing pinned-versions/seed config and absent 3rd-party replication as reliability floor failures.

satisfied: Programmatic, edge-case-aware scoring rules
0% unparseable outputs after the parser fix
gaps: No inter-rater kappa computed (open JAIST collaboration, 40-item sample)
correctness.justification: Scoring is machine-checkable and robust post-fix, but the paper requires rater-consistency evidence (kappa) for a top correctness grade.

satisfied: Expert-authored, precisely operationalized graduate-level questions
Broad subject coverage with well-specified single targets
Questions target genuine reasoning gaps, not guessing
construct_validity.justification: Closely matches the paper's construct-validity ideal: precise phenomenon, representative expert task space, verifiable targets. (Our 20-task trial is a sample, not the full 3k-item set.)

satisfied: Model isolated from ground truth (closed-book)
Deterministic exact/normalized grading
No MCQ guessing (open answer)
gaps: Single attempt per item in this trial; no per-item SE reported
internal_validity.justification: Isolation and grading are clean; the trial's single attempt per item is the only internal-validity deduction versus the published protocol.

satisfied: Drawn from real expert-domain tasks across many disciplines
Difficulty calibrated to exceed frontier-model capability
gaps: Our 20-task sample is not representative of the full distribution
external_validity.justification: Strong real-world expert grounding; sampling caveat applies only to this trial's downsampled set.

satisfied: Published protocol is replicable
Fixed task sample reused across models
gaps: No seeded run config / pinned model versions committed for this trial
reliability.justification: Replicable in principle; the trial run does not yet commit a full replication config (floor item for Cat A standing).

satisfied: Each question has a single verifiable target answer
Normalized answer matching handles formatting variance
correctness.justification: Ground truth is unambiguous and programmatically checkable — the paper's correctness ideal.

satisfied: Tasks map to real offensive-security skill areas (web/crypto/pwn/reverse/forensics)
Difficulty ladder present
gaps: Our 20 tasks are hand-authored trial samples, not the curated published repo tasks
Population not sampled from the published difficulty distribution
construct_validity.justification: Construct is right (real CTF skills), but the trial set is author-built rather than the vetted published corpus, so construct validity is a step below HLE.

satisfied: Flag is programmatic ground truth — no guessing path
Deterministic check
No MCQ
gaps: Single attempt per task in this trial
internal_validity.justification: Ground-truth isolation is excellent (a flag is either produced or not); single-attempt caveat only.

satisfied: Real CTF categories and realistic task framing
gaps: Difficulty/population not sampled from the published distribution
external_validity.justification: Genuine categories, but the trial sample is not drawn from the published task population.

satisfied: Reproducible given the fixed task set
Trivial-agent baseline (random guessing) ~0%
gaps: No committed replication config for the trial
reliability.justification: Reproducible in principle; trial lacks a committed config (floor item for Cat A).

satisfied: Each task has a verified end state (a known flag)
Scoring rule well-specified and handles edge cases
correctness.justification: Every task has an explicit solution to compare against — the paper's correctness ideal.
